classification.recommended_terminology: Lean-checked reconstruction of Erdős's no-coprimality extension at base two
nearest_prior_work: Erdős (1968/1969), p. 222, proves the pairwise-coprime reciprocal-summable theorem for every integer base t at least two.
The sentence following that theorem and the closing remarks on p. 226 state that pairwise coprimality can be dropped, while explicitly withholding the more complicated proof.

Kaneko-Suzuki-Tachiya (2026) give modern sparse-power-series criteria and a complete proof of a different omitted Erdős criterion; their framework is adjacent but does not state this Mersenne-support theorem.
Tao-Teräväinen (2025) prove the prime-support case by quantitative correlation methods; prime support lies outside the reciprocal-summable regime because the prime harmonic series diverges.
classification.attribution: Attribute the theorem statement to Erdős and the explicit base-two proof plus Lean verification to the local source. Do not imply that the proof recovers Erdős's unpublished argument.
classification.mathematical_interest: The theorem removes all mutual-coprimality structure from a broad sparse regime. Its proof replaces CRT separation by periodic atom averages and a recurrence obstruction, a mechanism different enough from the printed proof to be independently useful.
classification.reusable_scope: Infinite supports A with summable reciprocal conductor mass, at base two. More abstractly, positive periodic atoms admitting summable orbit-mean domination and a strict-minimum/close-return integer-gap endgame.
classification.why_it_matters: It is a genuine programme coverage theorem: every #257 attack on reciprocal-summable supports is already settled. The remaining frontier necessarily includes divergent reciprocal mass or seeks a different theorem that reaches it.

mechanism_comparison.printed_Erdos_mechanism: Under pairwise coprimality, CRT creates isolated nonzero base-t digits followed by arbitrarily long zero blocks, with reciprocal summability controlling tails.
mechanism_comparison.local_mechanism: At base two, shifted Mersenne atoms have explicit gcd-orbit means bounded by 1/d. Reciprocal summability supports LCM-prefix and Cesàro limits, producing a positive close return to the strict zero-shift minimum; rationality would turn that gap into an impossible integer strictly between zero and one.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: The local source supplies every omitted analytic and arithmetic step for base two without assuming pairwise coprimality.
mechanism_comparison.significance_boundary: This is a strong partial theorem for #257, but it does not reach primes or any support whose reciprocal mass diverges, and it does not prove the all-base extension.
